name: Avici
rootCause: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in an outdated version of Rain’s Solana card contract used by Avici (and a few other programs). By submitting crafted signature bundles to gain unauthorized admin rights via AddCollateralAdmin and then withdrawing collateral, they drained $500,859.22 from 1,685 users’ card balances. Self-custodial wallets were unaffected. The contract was upgraded across all programs, and full refunds were promised.

descriptions.text: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in an outdated version of Rain’s Solana card contract used by Avici (and a few other programs). By submitting crafted signature bundles to gain unauthorized admin rights via AddCollateralAdmin and then withdrawing collateral, they drained $500,859.22 from 1,685 users’ card balances. Self-custodial wallets were unaffected. The contract was upgraded across all programs, and full refunds were promised.

Avici’s Solana card contract was exploited on 2026-08-28, affecting 1,685 users and $500,859.22 in card balances. Public reports attribute the drain to an authorization flaw in an outdated Rain card contract that let the attacker register collateral-admin privileges and withdraw funds. Reported authorization and withdrawal-logic flaw in an outdated Rain Solana card contract used by Avici. Public reconstructions say the attacker reused a signature path to add collateral-admin authority and then withdraw card balances from affected accounts.
